title: Monarch butterfly
text: Monarchs from the northeastern United States and southeastern Canada travel 1,200 to 2,800 miles or more to the mountain forests of central Mexico, including the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve. No single butterfly flies the whole round trip; it takes several generations.
when: Monarchs head south in late summer and autumn, rest in Mexico from early November to mid-March, and their offspring come back north through spring and summer.
matters: Milkweed is the monarch caterpillar's only host plant. Its loss and climate change have disturbed breeding and migration, and numbers have fallen over the past two decades.
